sources.quote: When you cannot change lanes to pass a bicyclist, allow at least three feet between your vehicle and the bicyclist. If you cannot give three feet of space, do not pass the cyclist until three feet of clearance can be given. This will help you avoid putting the bicyclist in danger. Remember to:

sources.quote: Give bicyclists enough space so they are not forced into parked vehicles or open vehicle doors.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD merge [?safely] behind a cyclist WHEN about to make a turn

statements.note: Listed under "Passing a Bicyclist" after the lead "Remember to:" (p78); read as the driver merging behind the cyclist rather than passing when about to turn.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD approach or pass a cyclist on a two-lane road with [?extra care]

sources.quote: Be careful when approaching or passing a bicyclist on a two-lane road.

Drivers must move over and slow down for emergency and road work vehicles. These include:

statements.text: a driver SHOULD move to the right WHEN another driver is [?close] behind the driver AND the other driver wishes to drive faster

sources.quote: You must drive slower when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. At the same time, you should not block normal and reasonable traffic flow by driving too slowly. If you drive faster or slower than the speed limit, you may be cited. When another driver is close behind you and wishes to drive faster, move to the right. If you choose to drive slower than other traffic, drive in the right lane. Refer to Choosing a Lane in Section 6 for more information.

flags.note: No following distance is given.
p95 gives a similar duty to merge right and let a tailgater pass when safe.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD drive in the right-hand lane WHEN the driver chooses to drive slower than other traffic

sources.quote: You must drive slower when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. At the same time, you should not block normal and reasonable traffic flow by driving too slowly. If you drive faster or slower than the speed limit, you may be cited. When another driver is close behind you and wishes to drive faster, move to the right. If you choose to drive slower than other traffic, drive in the right lane. Refer to Choosing a Lane in Section 6 for more information.

flags.note: The "slower traffic keep right" sign in p42 states this as a sign rule.

statements.text: a driver MUST stop for a school bus

sources.quote: All vehicles must stop for school buses.
School bus with red lights flashing and a crossing guard next to it. Students are near the bus. Cars are stopped around the bus.

flags.span: All vehicles must stop for school buses
flags.note: p92 limits the duty to a school bus flashing its red lights, and p93 removes it across a divided or multilane highway.

statements.note: The passage states no condition; the figure shows a school bus with red lights flashing and cars stopped around it.

statements.text: a driver coming from either direction MUST stop WHEN a school bus is flashing its red lights at the top, front and back of the bus UNTIL the children are [?safely] across the street AND the red lights stop flashing IF VIOLATED a possible fine of up to $1,000 AND a possible licence suspension for 1 year

sources.quote: When the bus flashes red lights (located at the top, front, and back of the bus), you must stop from either direction until the children are safely across the street and the lights stop flashing. Remain stopped while the red lights are flashing. If you fail to stop, you may be fined up to $1,000 and your driving privilege could be suspended for one year.
The speed limit is 25 mph within 500 feet of a school while children are outside or crossing the street. Some school zones may have speed limits as low as 15 mph. When near schools, look for:
School bus with red lights flashing and a crossing guard next to it. Students are near the bus. Cars are stopped around the bus.

flags.note: The passage does not say when the children count as safely across.
The item sits under a list lead about being near schools, but its own wording does not depend on that, so the condition is not added.

statements.note: "May be fined" and "could be suspended" are kept as possible penalties; the driving privilege suspension is written as a licence suspension.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD remain stopped WHILE the red lights of a school bus are flashing

sources.quote: When the bus flashes red lights (located at the top, front, and back of the bus), you must stop from either direction until the children are safely across the street and the lights stop flashing. Remain stopped while the red lights are flashing. If you fail to stop, you may be fined up to $1,000 and your driving privilege could be suspended for one year.

flags.note: Follows "you must stop" about the same duty but is worded as an imperative.

statements.text: EXCEPTION TO p92a WHEN the school bus is on the other side of a divided or multi-lane highway with 2 or more lanes in each direction

sources.quote: If the school bus is on the other side of a divided or multilane highway (two or more lanes in each direction), you do not need to stop.

statements.note: The same exception also limits the unconditional duty in p90a.

statements.text: TO deal with a tailgater WHEN a tailgater is behind the driver

steps.text: create [?more space] in front of the vehicle
merge right into another lane AND allow the tailgater to pass WHEN it is [?safe to do so]

sources.quote: Create more space in front of your vehicle when:
A tailgater is behind you. Maintain your course and speed. Then, when safe to do so, merge right to change into another lane and allow the tailgater to pass.

flags.note: No amount of space is given.
The passage gives no test for when merging right is safe.

statements.note: Step 1 comes from the list lead (p94); the order of steps 2 and 3 comes from "Then".

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass traffic WHEN driving in heavy fog or smoke UNLESS passing is [?absolutely necessary]

sources.quote: Avoid crossing lanes or passing traffic unless absolutely necessary.
It is best to avoid driving in heavy fog or smoke. Consider postponing your trip until the fog clears. If you must drive in heavy fog or smoke:

flags.note: The passage does not say when passing becomes necessary.

statements.note: "Driving in heavy fog or smoke" comes from the list lead (p97); the advice on crossing lanes in the same sentence is outside the topic.

You should:

statements.text: FACT dangers are [?sometimes] on both sides of the road at the same time, such as parked cars to the right and oncoming cars to the left

sources.quote: Sometimes dangers will be on both sides of the road at the same time. For example, parked cars to the right and oncoming cars to the left.

flags.note: The handbook does not say how often this happens.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD give [?more space] to the most dangerous situation WHEN dangers are on both sides of the road AND one danger is [?greater] than the other

sources.quote: If one danger is greater than the other, give more space to the most dangerous situation. Suppose you are on a two-lane road with an oncoming vehicle to the left and a bicyclist ahead to your right. Instead of driving between the vehicle and the bicyclist, take one danger at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass. When the vehicle has passed, move to the left to allow plenty of space (at least three feet) to pass the bicyclist. If there is a steady flow of oncoming vehicles, use as much of the left lane as you safely can to pass the bicyclist.
Sometimes dangers will be on both sides of the road at the same time. For example, parked cars to the right and oncoming cars to the left.

flags.note: No amount of space is given.
The passage does not say how to judge which danger is greater.

statements.note: "Dangers on both sides of the road" comes from p102, whose example is passing parked cars with oncoming cars on the other side.

sources.quote: If one danger is greater than the other, give more space to the most dangerous situation.
